full_judgment: 14. It appears that the registered Bainanama Deed dated 10-4-2008 (Exhibit- 2) on which the plaintiff have based its claim in the present suit for Specific Performance of Contract. Admittedly, the defendant No. 1 is the executant of this Baina Deed. By this Bainanama, its executant, defendant No. 1 stipulated to sell to the plaintiff the suit schedules ‘ka’ and ‘kha’ land having an total area of 3.4764 acres fixing total price of the land at Taka 1,15,00,000. It was further stipulated in the Baina amongst others that defendant No. 1 received Taka 40,00,000 from the plaintiff as earnest money and agreed to execute necessary sale Deed /Deeds in favour of the plaintiff or its nominee and get it registered within 6 months from the date of the Bainanama Deed and balance consideration Taka 75,00,000 will be paid at the time of registration of the sale Deed. On the date of Bainanama, defendant No. 1 also delivered khas possession of the suit land. In the Bainanama it was further agreed that since the suit land was mortgaged to the defendant No. 3-Basic Bank Ltd., the defendant No.1 and 2 jointly execute a deed of agreement dated 10-4-2008 (Exhibit- 3) and in the said agreement it was stipulated that defendant No. 1 and her husband defendant No. 2 will redeem the mortgaged property by paying loan liability together with interest from their own source and at their responsibility within a period of 2 (two) months and furnished the original title deeds to the plaintiff-company. It is also stipulated that if the defendants fail and/or neglect to execute and register the Sale Deeds, the plaintiff will be entitled to obtain the deed through the process of the court.
